components.name: claude-opus-5-5
components.notes: claude-opus-5-5: input $4, output $20, 5-minute cache writes $5, 1-hour cache writes $8, cache hits $0.20 per million tokens; no long-context surcharge for Opus 5.5. Cache writes are priced at the 5-minute rate: it reproduces the harness-reported totals of dev runs 2 and 4 ($0.75, $0.77) within 3% (DECISIONS.md, Starwish dev runs), where the 1-hour rate would give about $0.92.
components.source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (Model pricing table, Claude Opus 5.5, read 2026-11-24; same figures on https://claude.com/pricing)

components.name: ElevenLabs (make-audio: voice and music)
components.notes: Per credit on Scale: $299 / 1,800,000 = $0.00016611. A video makes 2 calls (voice, then music). Credits per call are the tool caps, averaged: voice at most 540 characters = 540 credits (1 a character), music at most 22 + 8 = 30 s at about 15 credits a second = 450 credits; (540 + 450) / 2 = 495 credits = $0.0822 a call. Measured jobs used about 715-760 credits for the 2 calls (Task 12, Task 15, Task 13 estimates; the key cannot read its own usage), so this is a ceiling, about $0.04 a job above typical. The dollar list price on https://elevenlabs.io/pricing/api ($0.08 per 1,000 characters, music $0.15 a minute) gives about $0.10 a job, less again.
components.source: https://elevenlabs.io/pricing (Scale: $299 a month, 1.8M credits, read 2026-11-24); the creator: Scale plan (Yuki confirmed the plan is settled)

how_to_fill: Fill every unit_prices_usd value that is null, and source, for each component: look the price up on the provider's own pricing page (put the link in source) or ask the creator what they pay on their plan (source: "the creator: <plan>"). Never invent a price. Model prices are USD per million tokens of each kind; api is USD per call; subscription and resource are USD per request (0 when one request costs nothing extra, with the reason in notes). Add a component for any cost Starwish couldn't see, and add requests with observed: false and counted: true for heavier requests you expect (more input, more steps, retries, a cold cache), saying why in the label. A dev run that didn't complete with exit 0 has counted: false: its cost isn't what a request costs, so it's left out of the typical cost and the range. Then run `starwish price --worksheet <file>`.

platform.floor_rule: A price P (whole stars, at least 10) pays the creator P minus 10% of P rounded down; 1000 stars = $1. The floor for a cost of C dollars is the lowest P whose payout is at least C × 1000 (about C × 1000 ÷ 0.9). `starwish price --worksheet <file>` works it out from the AI's filled-in worksheet.

requests.label: heavy request (not observed): cold prompt cache, two frame-review rounds (three renders, a recorded clip re-recorded), two voice and two music calls. Tokens: above the highest of every run so far, local and on Starwish (the Task 14 local raycast.com run with a clip: 134,763 cache writes, 4,407,681 cache reads, 29,997 output, $2.16), plus 25,000 cache writes for a system prompt and tool list not yet cached (prompt.md is about 6,500 tokens; the preset adds its own).
